column2: A circumspect diplomat, he weighed every word before answering the reporter.
column3: 這位謹慎的外交官在回答記者之前，對每個字都再三斟酌。
column5: circum 周圍 + spect 看（inspect 檢查）：先看四周再行動

column2: Their promise of effortless wealth proved a chimera that vanished at the first audit.
column3: 他們輕鬆致富的承諾只是虛幻的空想，一經審計就煙消雲散。
column5: Chimera 是神話中獅頭羊身蛇尾的怪物，只存在想像裡
column8: 虛妄的幻想；空想；神話怪獸

column2: The taxi took a circuitous route through side streets, doubling the fare.
column3: 計程車繞了一條迂迴的路穿過小巷，車資因此多了一倍。
column5: circuit 是環路：沿著圓圈繞，就是不走直線

column2: Rather than say "fired," the manager resorted to circumlocution about "restructuring his future."
column3: 經理不直說「開除」，而是繞圈子講什麼「重整他的未來」。
column5: circum 周圍 + locu 說話（elocution 口才）：繞著圈說話
column8: 委婉曲折的說法；繞圈子說話

column2: Strict rules circumscribe what interns may do without supervision.
column3: 嚴格的規定限制了實習生在無人監督時能做的事。
column4: circumscribe one's powers (限制某人的權力)
column5: circum 周圍 + scribe 寫（describe 描述）：在四周畫一圈
column8: 限制；劃定界線；約束範圍

column2: Some firms circumvent tax laws by moving profits to countries with lower rates.
column3: 有些公司把利潤轉移到稅率較低的國家，以規避稅法。
column5: circum 周圍 + vent 來（prevent 預防）：繞過去走旁門
column8: 巧妙規避；繞過；鑽法律漏洞

column2: The two companies held clandestine talks in a hotel basement, hiding the meeting from regulators.
column3: 兩家公司在飯店地下室舉行祕密會談，向監管機關隱瞞這場會面。
column5: 想像躲在厚窗簾後面，壓低聲音偷偷談事情

column2: She cast a surreptitious glance at her phone during the lecture.
column3: 她在課堂上偷偷瞄了手機一眼。
column5: sur 在下面：像在桌子底下偷偷伸手，不讓人發現

column2: The cathedral and the nearby abbey are coeval, both completed around the year 1250.
column3: 這座大教堂與附近的修道院屬同一時代，兩者都在約一二五零年完工。
column4: coeval with the castle (與城堡同時代)
column5: co 一起 + ev 時代（medieval 中世紀）：活在同一個時代
column8: 同時代的；同時期的；同時代之人

column2: Her cogent argument persuaded even the most skeptical members of the board.
column3: 她令人信服的論述，連最持懷疑態度的董事也被說服了。
column5: co 一起 + gent 推動：把大家一起推向同意
column8: 令人信服；論述嚴密；強有力

column2: Regulators found evidence of collusion between the airlines to keep ticket prices high.
column3: 監管機構發現航空公司之間串通以維持高票價的證據。
column5: col 一起 + lus 玩（illusion 幻覺）：一起玩把戲

column2: Two bidders were suspected of colluding to drive down the price of the contract.
column3: 兩名投標者被懷疑串通，以壓低合約價格。
column4: collude with a rival (與對手串通)
column5: 跟 collusion 同家族：想像兩人躲在桌下偷偷擊掌

column2: Salary will be commensurate with experience, so senior applicants can expect higher offers.
column3: 薪資將與經驗相稱，因此資深的應徵者可期待更高的待遇。
column5: com 一起 + mensur 測量（measure）：量起來一樣大

column2: The punishment should be proportionate to the offense, not harsher than necessary.
column3: 處罰應與過錯相稱，不該比必要的更嚴厲。
column5: proportion 比例 + ate：比例剛剛好

column2: He felt no compunction about charging tourists triple the normal price.
column3: 他向觀光客收取三倍價格，內心毫無愧疚。
column5: com 加強 + punct 刺（puncture 戳破）：良心被針扎
column8: 良心不安；內疚；悔恨；歉意

column2: She had scruples about accepting an expensive gift from a client.
column3: 她對收下客戶送的昂貴禮物有所顧慮。
column5: 原指鞋裡的小尖石子：硌在腳上，良心也跟著不安
column8: 顧慮；道德疑慮；良心不安

column2: Rapid growth brought a concomitant rise in traffic and noise.
column3: 快速成長隨之帶來交通量與噪音的增加。
column5: con 一起 + comit 陪伴：一路相伴的跟班
column8: 相伴；伴隨；隨之而來；伴隨物

column2: The treaty restored concord between the two neighboring nations.
column3: 這項條約恢復了兩個鄰國之間的和睦。
column5: con 一起 + cord 心（cordial 熱誠）：心在一起

column2: The two triangles are congruent because all their sides and angles match exactly.
column3: 這兩個三角形全等，因為所有的邊和角都完全吻合。
column5: con 一起 + gru 相合：疊在一起剛好完全重合
column8: 一致；相符；吻合；幾何全等

column2: A true connoisseur of tea, she could name a leaf's region by its smell alone.
column3: 她是真正的茶葉鑑賞家，光憑氣味就能說出茶葉的產地。
column5: 諧音「康娜瘦」：看，那位 sir 是行家，一聞就知道

column2: A conscientious nurse, she double-checked every dose before going to the patient's bed.
column3: 她是認真負責的護理師，到病床前都會再三核對每一劑藥量。
column5: conscience 良心 + ious：憑良心把事情做好
column8: 認真負責；盡職盡責；本著良心

column2: A bright red umbrella was conspicuous in the gray crowd.
column3: 一把鮮紅色的雨傘在灰色的人群中格外醒目。
column5: con 全 + spic 看（inspect 檢查）：一眼就看見

column2: To the teacher's consternation, the whole class had forgotten the exam date.
column3: 令老師大為震驚的是，全班都忘了考試日期。
column5: 想像突然看到怪事，整個人僵在原地不知所措
column8: 驚惶失措；大為震驚；恐慌

column2: A consummate chef, she turned plain eggs into a dish that silenced the dining room.
column3: 她是技藝精湛的主廚，把普通雞蛋變成讓整間餐廳安靜下來的一道菜。
column5: con 全 + summ 頂點（summit 山頂）：爬到頂峰了
column8: 圓滿；技藝高超；精湛的；使圓滿

column2: He looked at the cheater with open contempt and walked out of the room.
column3: 他以毫不掩飾的蔑視看著作弊的人，然後走出房間。
column5: 想像抬高下巴，用鼻孔看人，一臉瞧不起

column2: She gave a contemptuous laugh when he claimed to be the best singer in town.
column3: 當他自稱是全鎮最會唱歌的人，她發出不屑的笑聲。
column5: contempt 蔑視 + uous 充滿：滿臉都是不屑

column2: Alaska is not part of the contiguous United States.
column3: 阿拉斯加不屬於美國本土相連的各州。
column5: con 一起 + tig 碰觸（contact 接觸）：邊挨著邊

column2: The contumacious defendant ignored the judge's order and refused to stand.
column3: 抗命的被告無視法官的命令，拒絕起立。
column5: 想像面對權威雙手抱胸，頭一偏就是不聽

column2: How to feed a growing city with shrinking farmland remains a conundrum for planners.
column3: 如何用日漸減少的農地養活成長中的城市，對規畫者仍是個難題。
column5: 諧音「肯那轉」：腦袋轉了又轉，還是解不開的謎
column8: 難題；謎語；令人困惑的謎題

column2: The painter remained an enigma; nobody knew where he lived or how he worked.
column3: 這位畫家始終是個謎；沒人知道他住在哪裡，或如何創作。
column5: 諧音「一泥個馬」：這到底是什麼馬？完全解不開
column8: 費解的人事物；神祕謎團

column2: Constant criticism can be corrosive to a team's trust.
column3: 不斷的批評會侵蝕團隊之間的信任。
column5: cor 全 + rod 啃咬（rodent 齧齒動物）：一點一點啃壞

column2: She was admitted to a small coterie of poets who met every Thursday.
column3: 她被接納進入一個每週四聚會的小詩人圈子。
column5: 想像幾個好友圍成小圈圈，外人擠不進來
column8: 小圈子；志同道合的小團體

column2: The school will not countenance bullying in any form.
column3: 學校不容許任何形式的霸凌。
column5: countenance 本是臉：肯給好臉色，就是贊同、容忍

column2: The general countermanded the retreat order moments before the troops began to move.
column3: 將軍在部隊開始移動前一刻，撤銷了撤退命令。
column5: counter 反 + mand 命令（command）：反過來下命令

column2: The agency ran a covert operation that was kept secret from Congress.
column3: 該機構執行了一項對國會保密的祕密行動。
column5: cover 蓋起來：蓋住不讓人看見

column2: Covetous neighbors eyed the old man's orchard and wondered how to get it.
column3: 貪婪的鄰居盯著老人的果園，盤算著怎麼弄到手。
column5: 想像眼睛直盯著別人的東西，口水快流下來
column8: 貪婪；覬覦他人之物；貪求

column2: The scam relied on the credulity of lonely retirees who trusted every caller.
column3: 這場詐騙仰賴孤單退休者的輕信，他們什麼來電都相信。
column5: cred 相信（credit 信用）：太容易就相信別人

column2: The culprit behind the blackout turned out to be a squirrel chewing on a cable.
column3: 造成停電的元兇，原來是一隻啃電纜的松鼠。
column4: find the culprit (找出罪魁禍首)
column5: 諧音「抗不利」：證據一出，犯人抗不過

column2: Budget cuts forced the library to curtail its weekend hours.
column3: 預算刪減迫使圖書館縮減週末的開放時間。
column5: 想像把 tail 尾巴剪短：長的東西被縮短
column8: 縮減；削減；剝奪；限制長度

column2: Environmental groups decried the plan to drain the wetland for a parking lot.
column3: 環保團體公開譴責把濕地排乾蓋停車場的計畫。
column5: de 向下 + cry 喊：大聲喊話把它貶低
